title: Integral-ideal filtrations on proper curves and their generic multiplicity profile
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then $X$ is Noetherian (locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, meaning every open cover has a finite subcover), and $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. There are finitely many dimension-one irreducible components [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Write them without repetitions as $C_1,\ldots,C_t$, each with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure [def-pc-reduced-scheme], and write $j_i:C_i\hookrightarrow X$ for its closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Each $C_i$ is integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], proper over $k$ and of dimension one, and has a unique generic point $\xi_i$ (viewed in $X$) with $\overline{\{\xi_i\}}=j_i(C_i)$. On any affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq X$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] meeting $C_i$, the reduced closed subscheme $C_i$ is cut out by the prime ideal of its underlying irreducible closed subset.

For every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F$ there is an integer $s\geq0$ and a filtration $0=\mathcal F_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal F_s=\mathcal F$ by coherent submodules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] whose quotients $\mathcal Q_a=\mathcal F_a/\mathcal F_{a-1}$ are isomorphic to $(h_a)_*\mathcal I_a$, for closed immersions $h_a:Z_a\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z_a$ integral and $\mathcal I_a\subseteq\mathcal O_{Z_a}$ a nonzero coherent ideal. Here the quotient is the cokernel of the inclusion and pushforward is pushforward of modules [def-pc-module-pullback]. Every $Z_a$ is proper over $k$ and Noetherian. For every filtration of this form, each $Z_a$ either has dimension zero and consists of a single closed point, or has dimension one and is equal, as a reduced closed subscheme of $X$, to exactly one $C_i$.

Put $R_i=\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}$ and let $\kappa(\xi_i)$ be its residue field [def-weil-residue-field]. For every such filtration, as $R_i$-modules the quotient stalk $(\mathcal Q_a)_{\xi_i}$ [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] is zero unless $h_a(Z_a)=j_i(C_i)$, and is $\kappa(\xi_i)$ when these supports agree; in the latter case $R_i\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_{C_i,\xi_i}=\kappa(\xi_i)$ is surjective and the quotient stalk has length one [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Consequently
$$\operatorname{length}_{R_i}(\mathcal F_{\xi_i})=\#\{a\in\{1,\ldots,s\}:h_a(Z_a)=j_i(C_i)\}<\infty.$$
In particular, when $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, each $m_i=\operatorname{length}_{R_i}R_i$ is a positive integer and equals this count. For $\mathcal F=0$ the length-zero filtration is allowed; if $X$ is empty then $\mathcal O_X=0$, the component list is empty and this filtration applies.

proof.text: The structure module $\mathcal O_Y$ of any scheme $Y$ is invertible: it is the rank-one free module, with its identity local trivializations. In particular take $\mathcal N=\mathcal O_X$ in [lem-trf-proper-field-invertible-coherent]. Its hypotheses are exactly that $k$ is a field and $X$ is proper over $k$; it gives Noetherianity of $X$ and coherence of $\mathcal O_X$. We will use the same application for any proper closed subscheme of $X$.

By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-components], select without repetitions the finite sublist of one-dimensional components. Give each its reduced induced structure using [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme]. Each resulting $C_i$ is nonempty, reduced and irreducible, hence integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme], and has the same dimension as its underlying component. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] it has a unique generic point $\xi_i$, whose closure in $X$ is its component. A nonempty open subset of an irreducible space is dense: two nonempty opens intersect, since otherwise their closed complements cover it. Thus on any affine open $U$ meeting this component, its intersection with $U$ is nonempty irreducible and closed in $U$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] it is $V(\mathfrak p)$ for a unique prime $\mathfrak p$. The radical-ideal description of the reduced induced structure identifies its defining ideal on $U$ with $\mathfrak p$.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes] to the Noetherian scheme $X$ of Step 1 and the given coherent module $\mathcal F$. It gives exactly the finite chain of coherent submodules, quotient cokernels, integral closed immersions $h_a$ and nonzero coherent ideals $\mathcal I_a$ asserted here. No dimension or reducedness hypothesis on $X$ is needed for this application. Fix any filtration with these properties for the remaining assertions, rather than just the one supplied by the existence theorem.

For every $h:Z\hookrightarrow X$ occurring in the filtration, and for every $j_i$, [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-proper] gives properness of the composite to $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Step 1 applied to each such proper scheme gives its Noetherianity. Write $T=h(Z)$, a nonempty irreducible closed subset of $X$. Chains of irreducible closed subsets of $T$ are chains in $X$, so $0\leq\dim T\leq1$ by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. If $\dim T=0$, the closure of every $x\in T$ equals $T$: a proper closure would give a chain of length one in $T$. Uniqueness of the generic point in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober] then says all its points coincide. It is a singleton closed in $X$. If $\dim T=1$, choose a nonempty irreducible closed $A\subsetneq T$ from a length-one chain. A strictly larger irreducible closed $W$ in $X$ would give $A\subsetneq T\subsetneq W$, contrary to $\dim X\leq1$. Thus $T$ is a component and equals exactly one listed component. Since $Z$ is integral, it is reduced, so uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-reduced-induced-closed-subscheme] identifies $h$ with that $j_i$ as a reduced closed subscheme. This also proves the claimed properness of each $C_i$.

source.place: Paragraph preceding Tag 0AYW (lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components); proper closed subschemes by morphisms.tex Tags 01W5 and 01W3; chain argument from topology.tex Tag 0055

proof.text: Fix $i$ and a factor indexed by $a$, and set $T_a=h_a(Z_a)$. If $\xi_i\in T_a$, closedness gives $j_i(C_i)=\overline{\{\xi_i\}}\subseteq T_a$. Since $T_a$ is irreducible and $j_i(C_i)$ is a maximal irreducible subset, equality follows by [def-weil-irreducible-components]. Consequently $T_a\neq j_i(C_i)$ implies $\xi_i\notin T_a$, and clause (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] gives $(\mathcal Q_a)_{\xi_i}=0$. If the supports agree, Step 4 identifies $Z_a$ with $C_i$ over $X$, and the point above $\xi_i$ is its generic point. We use this identification in the next step.

source.place: Tag 00AE (lemma-stalks-closed-pushforward), vanishing off the closed image; component maximality by topology.tex Tag 004V

proof.text: Suppose $T_a=j_i(C_i)$. The scheme $Z_a$ is Noetherian by Step 4, so [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth] makes its coherent ideal $\mathcal I_a$ quasi-coherent. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-integral-scheme-ideal-generic-stalk]: nonzeroness gives $(\mathcal I_a)_{\xi_i}=\mathcal O_{C_i,\xi_i}$ and this local ring is a field. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] identifies $(\mathcal Q_a)_{\xi_i}$ with this field as an $R_i$-module, with action through the immersion's stalk map. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], the structure-sheaf map onto $(j_i)_*\mathcal O_{C_i}$ is surjective; [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] and the same pushforward-stalk comparison therefore give a surjective local map $R_i\twoheadrightarrow\mathcal O_{C_i,\xi_i}$. Since the target is a field, the inverse image of its zero maximal ideal is the maximal ideal of $R_i$. Thus its kernel is that maximal ideal, so it identifies the target with $R_i/\mathfrak m_i=\kappa(\xi_i)$ by [def-weil-residue-field].

source.place: Tags 08KS (lemma-i-star-equivalence), generic stalk quotient-ring calculation, and 01AG (lemma-abelian); coherent.tex Tag 01XZ and generic ideal argument in Tag 01YL

proof.text: Through the surjection $R_i\twoheadrightarrow\kappa(\xi_i)$, every $R_i$-submodule of the residue field is stable under multiplication by every field element. A submodule containing $v\neq0$ contains $v^{-1}v=1$ and hence the whole field. Its only submodules are therefore $0$ and itself, and its length is one. The zero module has length zero, directly from [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. These conclusions are invariant under module isomorphism since an isomorphism and its inverse carry submodule chains to chains with the same strict inclusions. Steps 5 and 6 thus give quotient length $1$ precisely for the factors on $C_i$, and $0$ for all others.

source.place: Tag 02LY (definition-length); elementary submodule calculation for the residue-field module

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact] to each inclusion and its quotient cokernel. At $\xi_i$ this yields $0\to(\mathcal F_{a-1})_{\xi_i}\to(\mathcal F_a)_{\xi_i}\to(\mathcal Q_a)_{\xi_i}\to0$ over the same ring $R_i$. By [lem-weil-pbc-length-additive-short-exact], the length of the middle term is the sum of the other two. Starting from $(\mathcal F_0)_{\xi_i}=0$, induction on $a=0,\ldots,s$ gives length equal to the number of indices $b\leq a$ whose support is $C_i$: the base is zero and the successor adds exactly the indicator computed in Step 7. At $a=s$ this proves the asserted equality and finiteness for every filtration of the stated form.

source.place: Tag 00IV (lemma-length-additive); modules.tex Tag 01AG (lemma-abelian); generic multiplicity calculation preceding and in proof of varieties.tex Tag 0AYW

proof.text: For $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$, Step 1 supplies coherence and Step 8 supplies finite length and its equality with the count. The local ring $R_i$ is nonzero: it surjects onto the nonzero residue field. Hence $0\subsetneq R_i$ is a submodule chain of length one, so its finite length is positive by [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. For $\mathcal F=0$ choose $s=0$ and the chain with sole term $0$; there are no quotients to specify and every count and stalk length is zero. If $X$ is empty its structure sheaf is zero, the component list is empty, and this same chain applies.

from.place: The fibrewise ampleness-to-projectivity argument: positivity on normalized geometric-fibre components is converted to relative ampleness and then to a projective-bundle embedding. Supporting input: the proper integral curve degree criterion (0B5X). In the 0B5X proof this is the tensor-product degree formula used to pass from the degree of a positive tensor power to the degree of the line bundle and to obtain linear Euler-characteristic growth. Supporting input: the multiplicity-weighted reduction to reduced integral components in the proof of Stacks 0AYX (via 0AYW). Extraction: Original item proof steps 1 (Noetherianity and structure-module coherence), 2, 3, 4 and 5: coherent filtration, support geometry and generic length counts.
